subject: Information Theory
title: Interleaving
description: A quick, practical guide to Interleaving.

hook.text: A scratch on a CD destroys thousands of consecutive bits. Without interleaving, the error correction would fail.

buildup.text: Error-correcting codes handle scattered random errors well. Burst errors—long clusters—overwhelm them.

discovery.text: Interleaving shuffles data so consecutive bits come from different codewords. A burst error becomes spread out.

twist.text: After deinterleaving, each codeword sees only a few errors, not a concentrated burst. Standard codes handle it.

climax.text: CDs, DVDs, and digital TV all use interleaving. It turns the hardest error pattern into the easiest.

punchline.text: Scatter the data. Spread the burst. Let the code fix it.

quiz.question: What problem does interleaving solve?
options: Burst errors that overwhelm error-correcting codes
